title: Projects are now a conversation with Claude
format_note: Silent-on-voice, music-only walkthrough of one feature: messy requests become parallel threads, the user makes one design call, PRs land.
one_thing: You send scattered messages; Claude sorts them into parallel sessions and only asks you for the decisions.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. Captions hold only [music] tags and a few 'Woo!' lines (t=2, 5, 16, 25, 73) that cannot be confirmed as vocal.
transcript.script_shape: All meaning is on screen: five typed messages, a plan checklist, one choice thread, one feedback turn, a status list, a two-line tagline, then the product name.

structure.frame0: Dark ground with two grey chat bubbles in the middle, one tilted: 'click-through on the pricing page CTA has cratered…' and 'cold start is 4s??'. Subject present, nothing else.
structure.first_3s: Bubbles multiply to five, drift and tilt (t=0.2-3.5, window-01/02), then an orange asterisk and 'Untangling…' appear at t=4 (f0003).

beats.what: Five casual, typo-ridden requests pile up on black, tilting and shifting.

Pixel creature plus 'Claude', then tagline 'Claude runs the sessions. You make the calls.'
Orange dot grows to asterisk, wordmark types 'Claude Code', holds in silence.

hero_moment.what: Overview resets to 'Welcome back, Casey. Nothing is waiting on you.' with PR #9 and PR #4 ready for review (f0032).

ending.what: Tagline over pixel mascot (t=74-76.8), then a dot becomes the asterisk and 'Claude Code' types in, held 4.2 s with audio silent from 78.6 s.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Two long camera-move shots (7.25-41.33 s, 34 s, 41% of runtime) carry the story; cuts cluster as a 5-cut zoom burst at 60.08-64.79 s. Most change is on-screen state: bubbles, ticks, panels.

good.observation: The opening is the user's own messy words: five typed requests with typos, so the pain is shown rather than named, and the product's job reads before any UI.
One feature story is told as a loop: messages, plan, parallel threads, a design question, a one-line reply, PR landed. The user's role shrinks to decisions.
Real-looking UI is zoomed until text is large, so the key facts (A Ink, B Glow, C Card, option D, 'Nothing is waiting on you') are legible.
Abstract monospace diagram explains the architecture (three sessions, local vs remote) in one calm pass, with ticks as progress.
The ending is plain: a two-line tagline, then dot to asterisk to typed wordmark held 4.2 s in silence.
Colour is held back: near-black ground, one terracotta accent, saturation share 0.005, so each coloured item reads as Claude.

weak.observation: Nine-word opening title is visible about 1.9 s before a cut, too short to read comfortably and then the UI zoom replaces it.
Wide UI shots carry 9-12 px text that is unreadable on a phone, and the 'working' stretches repeat (24-36 s, 41 s of one chat).
Loudness misses the social targets: -15.5 LUFS and -0.8 dBTP, and cuts are not locked to the music.

rule_candidates.rule: Open with the user's real words as the problem: 2-5 typed messages with typos on a dark ground at frame 0, then add more by 3 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001 holds 2 bubbles; f0003 holds 5 by t=4

rule_candidates.rule: A film may run one continuous camera move over UI and diagram for over 30 s when on-screen state changes every 2-3 s; cut length is not the only pace.
rule_candidates.evidence: 7.25-41.33 s shot, 34 s, 41% runtime; median shot 4.17 s

rule_candidates.rule: A cut burst can land late: 5 cuts in 4.7 s at 75% of runtime, built from zoom-blur punches into the same UI, then the payoff screen.
Hold a 9-word title at least 3.2 s; this film shows its title about 1.9 s, which is too brief to read.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0004 at 6 s, cut at 7.25 s

rule_candidates.rule: Explain the mechanism with a monospace checklist of [ ] [~] [x] ticks and boxed sessions for 15-20 s when the real UI hides it; accept less real UI.
Show the user's role as one short typed reply that changes the outcome: feedback 'less might be more here' leads to a new option within 8 s.
End on a morph: a dot becomes the logo mark, the wordmark types on, and the last 4 s hold still; the audio may fall silent for those 4 s.
Keep the master at or below -14 LUFS and -1 dBTP; this film measures -15.5 LUFS and -0.8 dBTP, so check the final mix.
